title: fix(plugin-detail): record:details dedupes a titleFormat collapsed onto any field the template rendered
body:
Fixes #10360
Clause-②: no

## What

When no declared name pointer holds a value, the record page H1 is the rendered `titleFormat`. `record:details` hides the row whose value equals that rendered string, but it compared the string only against `titleCandidates`: the two ADR-0079 resolver rungs and six literal names. A template that collapsed onto any other field was not recognised. `{contract_no} - {name}` with a blank `name` put `HT-2026-003` in the H1 and again in the "Contract No" row directly under it.

The template-scan branch keeps the comparison and widens the set it compares against:

1. The candidate scan runs first, exactly as before, and a candidate match still wins. No row that was hidden before is hidden differently now.
2. Only when no candidate matches, the dedupe hides the first record field (in record key order) whose `recordDisplayValueAt` value EQUALS the rendered title AND that the template actually rendered. At most one row goes.

"Actually rendered" is asked of `formatTitleTemplate` itself: blank that one field on the record, render again, and see whether the title changed. There is no second placeholder parser.

objectui#8351 ruling B is kept: a row goes only on equality with the rendered string, never because a `titleFormat` exists. The declared-pointer branch (objectui#9436, landed in objectui#10358) and the empty-template walk are untouched.

## Mechanism assumptions, measured

- **A1 (reuse the renderer's placeholder parser): partly falsified, route changed.** `formatTitleTemplate` exports no parser. Its placeholder regexes are inline in the function body in `@object-ui/core`'s `record-title.ts`, so reusing them literally would mean a new `@object-ui/core` export, outside this claim's file surface. Instead the renderer itself is the oracle (blank and re-render). It therefore agrees by construction on every token shape `formatTitleTemplate` accepts: `{{field}}`, whitespace inside the braces, and dotted lookup paths such as `{account.name}`, where the record field blanked is the first path segment. No regex was written.
- **A2 (equality through `recordDisplayValueAt`, at most one row): confirmed. The example premise is falsified.** Two placeholders that both hold `HT-2026-003` do not collapse. Each renders its own copy, the H1 is `HT-2026-003 - HT-2026-003`, and both rows stay (pinned). Two TOP-LEVEL placeholder fields cannot both equal a collapsed title. The real two-equal case needs a dotted path. `{owner.nickname} - {rep}` with a blank nickname renders `rep`'s value, and an expanded `owner` whose display name is also `Ann` equals it too. The dedupe hides `rep`, because its placeholder rendered the H1. It keeps `owner`, because blanking `owner` leaves the title unchanged. A "first field the template names" rule would hide `owner` and keep the duplicate (pinned). If two fields both rendered the title AND both equal it, `.find` still hides only one: the first in record key order. That case needs two dotted lookups whose display names each equal the composite, so it is not pinned.
- **A3 (the objectui#8351 lit controls stay true): confirmed, no retarget.** `record-details.titleFormatNoDedupe-8351.test.tsx` is unchanged and green (10/10) under the fix and under the reverse proof.
- **A4 (only the template-scan branch moves): confirmed.** The change sits inside `if (interpolatedTitle)`, in the `else` that follows the declared-pointer check. The DECLARED POINTER CONTROL case pins that a template collapsing onto `contract_no` hides nothing while `nameField` holds a value.

## Tests

The new `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/__tests__/record-details.titleFormatPlaceholderDedupe-10360.test.tsx` renders the real `page:header` beside the real body under one record context, as the objectui#9436 agreement pin does. Each case reads the H1 the user sees and then which row drops. The viewport is pinned to desktop so that `DetailSection` auto-hide cannot remove a row.

- THE CARD: the H1 is `HT-2026-003`. The body has no `HT-2026-003` and no "Contract No".
- COMPOSITE CONTROL: the H1 is `HT-2026-013 - Acme Corporation`, and both rows stay.
- SAME VALUE IN BOTH PLACEHOLDERS: the H1 is a composite, and both rows stay.
- TWO FIELDS EQUAL THE H1: `rep` goes, and the derived `name` row stays.
- DECLARED POINTER CONTROL: only the pointer's row goes, and `contract_no` stays.

**Red on base `c3025ead2`, before the fix.** THE CARD and TWO FIELDS EQUAL fail; the first message is `expected 'Contract NoHT-2026-003Name—Amount13' not to contain 'HT-2026-003'`. The other 3 cases pass. The H1 assertions pass on base, so the header really shows what the card says.

**Reverse proof.** Run on the committed fix with `ablation-replace.mjs` in WRAP mode. Each restore was proven by blob == HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`.

- Restoring the candidate-only comparison turns THE CARD and TWO FIELDS EQUAL red (2 failed, 16 passed). COMPOSITE, SAME VALUE, DECLARED POINTER, all 10 cases of the objectui#8351 file and all 3 of the objectui#9436 agreement file stay green.
- Dropping only the "the template actually rendered it" check turns TWO FIELDS EQUAL red. The other 4 cases stay green.

The subject is imported by relative path from `src`, so neither leg needed a build.

## Gates, at HEAD `84039bba8`

- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/plugin-detail/ packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/column-identity.ratchet.test.ts packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/record-title` exited 0: 211 files (210 passed, 1 skipped), 2159 tests passed and 8 skipped. The run covers every `record-details*` suite. It also covers the source-text pins that read `record-details.tsx`: `recordDetailsInputs.spec-parity`, `detailRendererUndeclaredKeys-8649` and `column-identity.ratchet`.
- The closure build `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter "@object-ui/plugin-detail^..." build` exited 0. It built 11 packages; `test-support` has no build script.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-detail build` exited 0. That is vite plus the dts plugin, which fails on type errors.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-detail type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) exited 0. `--listFilesOnly` confirms that the test project includes the new file and the objectui#8351 file.
- The changeset gates all exited 0: `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-overwrite`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check:changeset-claims` and `check:pending-changeset-literals`. `check:changeset-claims` is report-only. It flagged 3 pending changesets, `7997-detail-view-related-retired`, `8400-kanban-name-field-skip-set` and `8649-detail-renderer-undeclared-keys`. I read each one whole, and all three are still true against this diff.
- `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check:control-bytes`, `check:test-path-roots` and `check:unreferenced-sources` all exited 0.
- ESLint on the 2 touched TS files found 0 errors. `record-details.tsx` has 35 warnings, the same as base. The new test has 2 `no-explicit-any` warnings, from the same helper signature the objectui#9436 pin uses. The narrowing rests on three facts:
  - The population is the plugin-detail `lint` script, `eslint .`, under the root `eslint.config.js`.
  - The file count is 2, read from `--format json`.
  - No type-aware linting is configured (no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`), and no custom rule in `eslint-rules/` reads other files. So this diff cannot move any untouched file's verdict.

Left to CI: the full `pnpm test` shards, repo-wide `pnpm type-check`, `pnpm lint`, the `pnpm check` CLI self-check, and Build & E2E.

## Acceptance notes

- **Reported to the seat for filing, not filed here (class a).** The page header and this dedupe render `titleFormat` through two different functions. The header uses `PageHeaderRenderer`'s own `interpolate` plus `cleanupTitleSeparators`; its comment records that it kept these in objectui#9436. The dedupe, `getRecordDisplayName` and `DetailView` use core's `formatTitleTemplate`. Both cases below were measured on this branch, and in each a duplicate row survives that the widened scan cannot see:
  - With a whitespace-only `name`, the H1 is `HT-2026-003` but core renders `HT-2026-003 -`, so the body still prints `HT-2026-003`. `getRecordDisplayName` also returns `HT-2026-003 -`.
  - With `{account} - {deal_no}` and an expanded `account`, the H1 is `Q3-042` but core renders `Acme - Q3-042`, so the body prints `Q3-042`.
- The pending objectui#8351 changeset says the dedupe answers "whether that string is some candidate's value". That is still true of the first step. This PR's changeset, in the same release, describes the widened second step.
- Whether a collapsed template should be the H1 at all is still out of scope (triage note 3).
